partners.diseaseBName: congenital disorder of glycosylation, type ICC
partners.mechanism_chain: TUSC3 (HGNC:12102) —DISRUPTS→ N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486); N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); MAGT1 (HGNC:23990) —DISRUPTS→ N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486); N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263). partners.mechanism_chain: TUSC3 (HGNC:24084) —DISRUPTS→ ER-Golgi transport (GO:0006888); ER-Golgi transport (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital disorder of glycosylation type I (MONDO:0012615); NIPA1 (HGNC:17734) —DISRUPTS→ Golgi apparatus homeostasis (GO:0005795); Golgi apparatus homeostasis (GO:0005795) —LEADS_TO→ Hereditary spastic paraplegia 6 (MONDO:0010878); ER-Golgi transport (GO:0006888) —BINDS→ Golgi apparatus homeostasis (GO:0005795). Loss-of-function mutations in TUSC3 disrupt ER-Golgi transport, leading to Congenital disorder of glycosylation type I. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in NIPA1 disrupt Golgi apparatus homeostasis. ER-Golgi transport is intrinsically linked to the maintenance and function of the Golgi apparatus. Therefore, both pathways converge on the integrity and function of the Golgi apparatus, a shared cellular compartment critical for protein modification and trafficking, ultimately manifesting as distinct neurological and systemic phenotypes.

partners.mechanism_chain: TUSC3 (HGNC:12447) —DISRUPTS→ ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030439); ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030439) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cellular response to ER stress (HP:0011021); CTNS (HGNC:2556) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal cystine transport (GO:0000103); Cystine (CHEBI:17600) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosomal cystine transport (GO:0000103); Lysosomal cystine transport (GO:0000103) —LEADS_TO→ Nephropathic cystinosis (HP:0000056). Loss-of-function mutations in TUSC3 disrupt the ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) pathway, leading to abnormal cellular responses to ER stress. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in CTNS impair lysosomal cystine transport, causing cystinosis. The convergence is proposed through the shared cellular stress response mechanisms affected by ERAD dysfunction and lysosomal dysfunction, potentially impacting cellular homeostasis and organelle integrity, which are fundamental to both disease pathologies.

partners.mechanism_chain: TUSC3 (HGNC:12486) —DISRUPTS→ Lipid metabolism (GO:0006629); Lipid metabolism (GO:0006629) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); NIPAL4 (HGNC:29987) —DISRUPTS→ Sphingolipid metabolism (GO:0006664); Sphingolipid metabolism (GO:0006664) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital ichthyosis (HP:0001072). partners.mechanism_chain: LRRC8A (HGNC:24996) —DISRUPTS→ Volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC) activity (GO:0099532); Volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC) activity (GO:0099532) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired B cell development and function (HP:0004790); Volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC) activity (GO:0099532) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cellular swelling/shrinkage response (HP:0033743).
